data.content_ref: inline:The problem asks why the air in a large city stays warmer on a clear, calm night. The target's entire mechanism hinges on reduced wind speed decoupling the city from the regional atmosphere. But 'clear, calm night' already implies low wind, so reduced wind speed cannot be the single mechanism that explains the urban–rural gap under the stated conditions; the target also fails to identify the dominant nocturnal cause (longwave radiative exchange/sky view factor) and offers no first-order reason rural air would cool faster than urban air when both are calm.
